name: (E)-2,6-Dimethyl-1,5,7-octatrien-3-ol
evidence: Measured in 3 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.06–0.09% of total volatiles (0.012–0.018mg per chew).

consumer_summary.what_it_is: A volatile monoterpene alcohol, (E)-2,6-dimethyl-1,5,7-octatrien-3-ol is one of the many aromatic molecules that give certain wild shrubs their distinctive, earthy scent. People are most likely to encounter it when brushing past or brewing traditional teas from wild marsh plants.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in several aromatic shrubs of the heather family, including wild rosemary (Ledum palustre) and bog Labrador tea (Rhododendron groenlandicum).
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: While this specific molecule has not yet been the focus of dedicated pharmacological studies, researchers are interested in the complex chemical makeup of the traditional medicinal plants it inhabits. Currently, there is no formal evidence (Oxford level 5, none found) detailing its individual effects, but cataloging compounds like this helps scientists understand the full aromatic and chemical profile of wild botanicals.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: There is currently no published evidence (Oxford level 5) evaluating the health effects of this specific molecule.
